title: Reflexive Verbs
summary: Using reflexive verbs in everyday contexts and talking about habits and reactions.
whyItMatters: Reflexive verbs describe routines, feelings, interests, memories, and reciprocal actions that are common in everyday conversation.

mentalModel.title: The pronoun points back to the subject
mentalModel.content: Ich freue mich and du freust dich use a reflexive pronoun matching the subject.

mentalModel.title: Learn the verb with its pattern
mentalModel.content: Some verbs are always or commonly reflexive and may require a fixed preposition.

ruleBlocks.title: Match the reflexive pronoun
ruleBlocks.content: Use mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich for accusative reflexive forms.

ruleBlocks.title: Recognize dative reflexives
ruleBlocks.content: When another accusative object appears, use mir or dir: Ich sehe mir den Film an.

ruleBlocks.title: Learn fixed complements
ruleBlocks.content: Practice sich interessieren für, sich freuen auf/über, and sich erinnern an.

tables.title: Reflexive Patterns
rows: Ich sehe mir die Serie an.
Sie erinnert sich an die Szene.

examples.de: Ich interessiere mich besonders für Dokumentarfilme.
examples.en: I am especially interested in documentaries.

examples.de: Wir sehen uns heute Abend einen Film an.
examples.en: We are watching a film this evening.

examples.de: Er erinnert sich noch gut an das Ende.
examples.en: He still remembers the ending well.

commonMistakes.reason: The verb requires a reflexive pronoun and für.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ich sehe mich den Film an.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich sehe mir den Film an.
commonMistakes.reason: The film is the accusative object, so the reflexive pronoun is dative.

comparisons.summary: Media habits and reactions provide natural reflexive contexts.
Reflexive verbs help express interest, memory, and emotional response.
